source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Unfasten and peel the gown away from the body, turn it inside out, roll it into a bundle, and then perform hand hygiene.","B":"Pull the gown forward by its contaminated front panel, keeping the outer surface against clothing and skin during removal.","C":"Wear the used gown to the nursing station, then remove it after touching shared equipment outside the patient area.","D":"Shake the gown vigorously before disposal, because aerosolizing surface contamination helps separate the sleeves."}}
source_row.rationale: Gown doffing should minimize contact with the contaminated outer surface and turn the gown inward while keeping contamination away from skin and clothing; exact doffing sequence may vary by PPE ensemble/protocol.
source_row.source_detail: PPE removal principles: remove and discard contaminated PPE to prevent contamination of clothing, skin or mucous membranes; gown removal turns the contaminated surface inward and avoids touching exposed surfaces. Current CDC Isolation Precautions prevention guidance rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: When removing a contaminated isolation gown, which technique best reduces self-contamination?
